subsequent_approved_deltas.verification: The diff in both files is additive CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS statements inside the existing schema executescript, plus comments: 38 inserted lines and 0 deleted across the two. services/native_price_action.py, services/native_smc.py and services/mtf_policy.py still hash to their PR #6 baseline values. An index changes how SQLite reaches rows, never which rows it returns or in what order, and the queries themselves are byte-identical; tests/test_lab_status_reads_are_indexed.py asserts both the new access paths and that state() still answers the same shape.

subsequent_approved_deltas.delta: Bound the per-collection reads in each lab's state() and report exact totals from COUNT(*) alongside the returned window; call state() once rather than N+2 times in the SMC metrics summary; and stop PriceActionPaperAccount.live_state presenting a freshly constructed empty engine as though it were the worker's. Read-path, aggregation and reporting only.
subsequent_approved_deltas.verification: services/native_price_action.py, services/native_smc.py and services/mtf_policy.py still hash to their PR #6 baseline values, so entry conditions, stop model, target R and the native MTF policy are untouched. 91 inserted and 20 deleted lines across the two lab modules. The queries are byte-identical apart from an appended LIMIT on four PA collections (pa_candidates, pa_order_meta, pa_funding_events, pa_position_remediations) and three SMC ones (smc_order_meta, smc_candidates, smc_funding_events); their siblings pa_activity, pa_evaluations, smc_activity and the broker fills were already capped the same way. Every caller that needs a whole collection passes limit=None, and counts that were previously len() of an unbounded read now come from COUNT(*), so orders_placed and target_1_hits are unchanged. No decision, proposal, sizing or fill path was modified. Motivation was a production incident: two lab sessions left open since 2026-08-24 and 2026-09-03 made state() re-materialise whole sessions on every tick and status poll, at ~30 MB/s memory growth with a core pegged, until the container reached its 11.4 GB ceiling.
